subsystems.name: Drilling vessel and riser
subsystems.role: reaches the seafloor and keeps a closed, controllable hole through kilometres of water.

subsystems.name: Core recovery
subsystems.role: cuts and lifts intact cylinders of sediment, rock and basalt.

subsystems.name: Contamination control
subsystems.role: proves that recovered microbes came from the formation, not the drilling fluid.

subsystems.name: Anaerobic handling
subsystems.role: keeps oxygen-sensitive subsurface samples chemically unchanged.

subsystems.name: Microbiology and geochemistry laboratories
subsystems.role: measures how many cells are present and what they eat.

subsystems.name: Downhole logging and observatories
subsystems.role: measures the formation and fluid in place, and monitors it for years afterwards.

subsystems.name: Metagenomics
subsystems.role: reads the DNA of communities that mostly cannot be cultured.

buildSteps.title: Select the site
buildSteps.detail: Seismic reflection surveys and thermal models identify sediment or fractured rock where fluids circulate and organic matter or hydrogen is available.

buildSteps.title: Drill and core
buildSteps.detail: The ship holds position over the hole while a piston corer takes the uppermost soft sediment and rotary coring cuts harder layers and basalt below.

buildSteps.title: Trace contamination
buildSteps.detail: Tracer is added to the drilling fluid; only intervals with tracer below a set threshold are treated as uncontaminated.

buildSteps.title: Process cores without oxygen
buildSteps.detail: Cores are cut and subsampled inside a glove box under inert gas within hours, then stored chilled or frozen.

buildSteps.title: Count cells and read chemistry
buildSteps.detail: Subsamples are fixed for microscopy and flow cytometry, while porewater is squeezed for ions, gases and isotopes to reconstruct the energy budget.

buildSteps.title: Sequence and culture
buildSteps.detail: DNA is extracted and sequenced to reconstruct genomes; selected samples are incubated in high-pressure vessels to test what actually grows.

buildSteps.title: Install observatories
buildSteps.detail: A borehole observatory is sealed into the hole with packers so fluid chemistry and temperature can be logged long after the ship leaves.

buildSteps.title: Compare with planetary analogues
buildSteps.detail: Results set the temperature, pressure and energy limits for life without sunlight, which are then applied to Mars, Europa and Enceladus.

prerequisites.why: only a few vessels can core in kilometres of water and recover uncontaminated samples.
subsurface cell densities are so low that a trace of drilling fluid would swamp the signal.
samples contain picograms of DNA, so extraction blanks and controls are essential.
most subsurface microbes have never been grown, because they need pressures and temperatures hard to reproduce in a lab.
drilling disturbs the hole, so in-place conditions must be measured after it settles.

pathway.milestone: scientific ocean drilling and continental boreholes recovering microbes from sediments and fractured rock kilometres down
pathway.unlocks: hard limits on temperature, pressure and energy supply for life without photosynthesis.

pathway.milestone: cleaner dedicated deep-biosphere drilling with routine anaerobic sampling and tracers
pathway.unlocks: a reliable census of how much biomass exists below the seafloor and continents.

pathway.milestone: linked networks of borehole observatories with in-situ experiments
pathway.unlocks: watching subsurface communities respond over years, rather than from one snapshot core.

pathway.milestone: analogue criteria applied to ocean-world missions
pathway.unlocks: targeted searches for life under the ice of Europa and in Enceladus plumes.
